target_customer: Chemical makers, ethanol producers and consumer brands wanting bio-based acrylic acid and related materials
problem: Chemicals are made from petroleum or from sugar-based processes that are costly; engineered microbes using cheaper feedstocks such as methane or ethanol could make greener chemicals at lower cost.
business_model: Technology development and partnership model: provides strain, bioprocess, samples and IP while partners co-develop and commercialize (per company site)

founders.name: Derek Greenfield
education: PhD (institution not specified; the founders hold PhDs from Stanford, UC Berkeley and UCSF per TechCrunch)
founders.background_notes: Synthetic biologist who met co-founders at LS9.

founders.name: Noah Helman
founders.role: CEO per 2024 press release (YC page: CSO)

competitors.name: LS9
competitors.what: Synthetic biology biofuels and chemicals company that relied on sugar feedstocks; the founders' former employer, presented by TechCrunch as a cautionary comparison
competitors.traction_then: Had been sold for up to $61.5 million
competitors.funding_then: More than $80 million in venture investment

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering microbes to convert methane or ethanol into chemicals and scaling fermentation and purification is research-grade, and took nine years to reach 20 kg batches.

defensibility.rationale: Company reports 22 to 23 patents and specialized strains and processes that are hard to replicate, but commercial scale is unproven.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Other synthetic biology firms pursued bio-based chemicals; none acquired it. A 2024 C&EN article says the sector has underperformed on its promises.

market_need_then: Interest in lower-carbon chemicals and cheaper feedstocks, with half a billion dollars invested in synthetic biology companies in 2015 (SynBioBeta). The founders' prior employer LS9 showed sugar based processes struggled on cost.

branding.domain_note: Uses imicrobes.com with the short brand iMicrobes; no purchase history found.

identity.logo: A profile describes a black wordmark; an automated homepage description mentions a globe icon in a circle (low confidence)
identity.visual_style: Green, white, brown and black palette per automated description

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive name with a shortened alias; no evidence the brand drove awareness or hiring.

outcome_analysis: Industrial Microbes is still a research-heavy company nine years in. It moved biobased acrylic acid from gram scale to 20 kg batches by September 2025 and closed a seed round led by First Bight in November 2024 that took total investment past $10M. The long timeline and small funding reflect the technical difficulty of industrial biotech; no exit or failure has occurred.
notes: Company states total investment exceeds $10M after the first close; the round size is not stated separately, so amount is null. Aggregators list a $120K pre-seed (YC) and a National Science Foundation grant (Employbl), $2.87M over 8 rounds (CB Insights) and $11.52M (Caplight); unverified and not recorded. Titles conflict: YC page says Greenfield is CEO and Helman CSO; the 2024 release says Helman CEO and Greenfield President. Outcome search found no acquisition, shutdown or layoffs. The TechCrunch article also names Counsyl and 20n as peers, not competitors. Which degree each founder holds is not stated.
